findings.source_line: P1 lib/agent-core/thread-find-or-create.ts:78-83 (threadNamesSomeoneElse), set by thread-store.ts linkThreadClient and handle-turn.ts:560/:867 — a thread carrying the clientLinkedInConversation marker is never split when the number later becomes shared, so on SMS and WhatsApp the shared-number texter's message is filed on client A's thread (client_id stays A, status stays active) AND listThreadMessages (handle-turn.ts:555) feeds A's earlier AI replies (name, booked treatment) to the model. Real scenario: a new patient texts from an unlisted mobile, the AI books her (marker set), later her daughter is booked on the same mobile (two live clients, lookup ambiguous); the daughter's next text is answered with the mother's thread history in the prompt and lands on the mother's record. Reproduced on pg with a scratch test (history row 'Hi Philippa Quartermaine, you are booked for Zygomatic Lift Deluxe'): SMS shared, SMS deleted twin and WhatsApp shared all leave the one thread on client-a, 4 messages, active, and the model input contains the surname and the booking text; the unmarked control splits correctly. The branch's own marker test uses a history row with no client data so it cannot see this — fix: keep the marker exception only when the number names nobody (numberUnknown) and always split a marked thread when lookup is ambiguous or deleted, plus a pg test with realistic AI-reply history asserting the model input is free of A's name

findings.source_line: P2 lib/agent-core/thread-find-or-create.ts:78 — threadNamesSomeoneElse returns false for any thread whose status is not `active`, so an `escalated` or `human_handling` thread is never left behind when the number now belongs to someone else (bead promise: "the message is no longer filed on the earlier client's thread"). Reproduced on Postgres (scratch cells OPUS-1 SMS/escalated, OPUS-2 WhatsApp/human_handling): A's number moved to new sole client C, C texts "Hi it's Cara" → stored as message 2 on A's thread `conv-a-sms-1` (client_id client-a, still escalated); same on WhatsApp/human_handling. Prod read (prod-sql.sh, 23 Oct): all 4 open escalated/human_handling SMS threads are client-linked, 3 have had no message for over 14 days, and staff have resolved 1 of 22 concierge threads ever. So these threads stay open indefinitely. Clinic scenario: a client's AI conversation ended in "let me get the team to call you" weeks ago, and nobody clicked resolve in Front Desk. The clinic later gives her old mobile to a new client, or adds a daughter on the family phone. On a weekday morning the new person texts the clinic. Reception sees the text in Front Desk under the old client's name and history and replies from that thread. The new person's message is now part of the old client's record (erased with her, kept on her history), which is the r8 recycled-number complaint this bead was filed for. Carve-out: patient data, and the wrong name is shown to staff. Fix: when a non-active thread names someone else (a different sole client, or identityUnknown without the in-conversation marker), keep it open so the Front Desk item is not cleared. Insert a new thread for this turn (client_id = the turn's sole client or null) instead of returning the old one; findOrCreateThread already picks the newest open thread by lastMessageAt. Add pg cells for recycled and shared numbers × escalated and human_handling. The current cell "a thread waiting for staff is never closed" should assert the text lands on the new thread and the old one stays open.

When the turn's clientId is null, resolveConciergeEmailRecipient falls back to `eq(clients.phone, from)` with no deletedAt filter (limit 2). findings.source_line: P3 lib/agent-core/gateways/whatsapp.ts:168-180 — WhatsApp still computes the texter's identity inline (`identityUnknown: !clientId`) instead of through the new texterIdentity, so it never sets numberUnknown. A client the AI booked by name from a number that is on nobody's record stays herself on her next SMS (turnClientId honours the marker) but becomes nobody on her next WhatsApp. That matches main for WhatsApp, and no data is exposed, but the two channels now answer the same person differently. Not graded H-D0: both paths reduce to lookupCaller/soleLiveClient, so there is no second ownership rule. Fix: call texterIdentity(undefined, phone, businessId) in runWhatsAppConcierge.

findings.source_line: P3 lib/agent-core/thread-find-or-create.ts:76 — cross-branch, for whichever of z0ote/hgyyd lands second. hgyyd's softDeleteClient → keepSharedNumberWhatsApp (lib/clients/soft-delete-client.ts on origin/goal/aestheticcnext-hgyyd) sets client_id to null on a WhatsApp thread that a remaining family member's number still holds. threadNamesSomeoneElse never splits a client_id-null thread, and the deleted record still makes the number `ambiguous`. So the remaining family member's next WhatsApp continues on the deleted client's thread, with her last 24 messages in the AI's history (listThreadMessages). It is the same family handset, so the messages are already on the device, and no other data reaches the model. Fix: add a pg cell on the combined tree, or have hgyyd resolve the kept thread instead of nulling it. Separately, for hgyyd's reviewer (not this branch): anotherLiveClientHoldsNumber in lib/concierge/live-number-holder.ts re-implements findClientsByExactPhone's prefilter + isExactPhone with a live-only filter. It could be `findClientsByExactPhone(...).some(c => !c.isDeleted && c.id !== clientId)` (it would need a tx parameter). That is a possible H-D0 on hgyyd.

findings.source_line: P3 lib/agent-core/thread-find-or-create.ts:160 — Scenario: a mum (client A) and her daughter (client B) share a family mobile. Mum's SMS thread is in human_handling. On a weekday afternoon, reception at the desktop Front Desk replies to mum inside her own client item, which writes to A's held thread and bumps its last_message_at. Mum texts back "Tuesday is great thanks". Because the number is shared, the turn has no identity. The newest open thread is again A's held thread, so findOrCreateThread inserts another client-less escalated thread instead of reusing the one the family's first text already opened. Every round trip of "staff reply on A's item, then a family text" adds one more held conversation row. On pg (scratch cell OPUSR2-1, staff reply stamped +1s), two family texts gave A's thread plus three client-less escalated rows, one of them empty. The empty row comes from runAgentLoop's second findOrCreateTurnThread call (handle-turn.ts:483) seeing A's thread still newest. Without the +1s skew the trace gives one extra row per exchange. No client data is exposed and the AI stays quiet, as intended. Each row is one more held conversation for staff to resolve (adjacent to nvt2y/iiqyh). Whether Front Desk shows the rows as one phone-keyed item or several is not verified. — Fix: in the held branch, before inserting, reuse the newest open thread on the number that does not name someone else (e.g. an open HELD_NUMBER_NEW_THREAD_REASON thread). Have runAgentLoop take the conversation handleTurn already resolved instead of calling findOrCreateTurnThread a second time.

findings.source_line: P3 lib/agent-core/thread-find-or-create.ts:149 — reproduced on pg (scratch S2): A's SMS thread is escalated, B is given A's number, and the new person texts, so a new escalated Front Desk thread opens. Reception then replies on A's held thread, which moves its last_message_at ahead of the new thread. The new person texts again and findOrCreateThread picks A's held thread as newest, splits again, and opens a third escalated thread. Result: reception sees two Front Desk items for one person on weekday mornings. No A data reaches the model or the new person, so this is a nuisance only — fix: when the newest open thread is held and names someone else, look for an open client-less or same-client thread for this number before inserting, or order the pick by newest non-held thread.
